pamphlet_excerpts: Healthy Aquatic Animal Colonies: Aquaculture medicine uses the principles of veterinary medicine to maintain healthy colonies of fish and other aquatic animals (p. 22).
Distinction From Marine Biology: This field of veterinary medicine is distinct from other areas of aquatic science, such as marine biology (p. 22).
Global Food Supply Role: As the world population grows, aquaculture will help provide an adequate food supply, and the work of aquaculture veterinarians will be critical (p. 22).
Veterinary Doctorate Degree Requirement: Students interested in aquaculture medicine must earn a doctorate in veterinary medicine (p. 22).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Support Global Food Production: As the world population grows, aquaculture will help provide an adequate food supply, and the work of aquaculture veterinarians will be critical (p. 22).
Step 2 - Earn a Veterinary Doctorate: Students interested in aquaculture medicine must earn a doctorate in veterinary medicine (p. 22).
Step 3 - Complete Specialized Postgraduate Training: Postgraduate training in aquaculture medicine is offered at some schools of veterinary medicine (p. 22).
Step 4 - Pursue Expanding Aquaculture Careers: Many opportunities, especially in the coming years, await individuals trained in aquaculture medicine (p. 22).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Beyond treating sick pets in a clinic, how do veterinarians protect human public health and the nation's food supply?
quiz_item.question: Beyond treating sick pets in a clinic, how do veterinarians protect human public health and the nation's food supply?
options: A. By prescribing human antibiotics to grocery store produce departments.
B. By controlling zoonotic diseases (such as rabies, brucellosis, and avian influenza) that can pass from animals to humans, and inspecting livestock health and food safety from farm to table.
C. By breeding wild predators to replace domestic cattle and poultry on commercial ranches.
D. By restricting vaccinations exclusively to indoor house cats and ornamental aquarium fish.
choices: A. By prescribing human antibiotics to grocery store produce departments.
B. By controlling zoonotic diseases (such as rabies, brucellosis, and avian influenza) that can pass from animals to humans, and inspecting livestock health and food safety from farm to table.
C. By breeding wild predators to replace domestic cattle and poultry on commercial ranches.
D. By restricting vaccinations exclusively to indoor house cats and ornamental aquarium fish.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. By controlling zoonotic diseases (such as rabies, brucellosis, and avian influenza) that can pass from animals to humans, and inspecting livestock health and food safety from farm to table.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Veterinarians play a vital One Health role by preventing zoonotic disease spill over between animals and people (such as rabies vaccination) and safeguarding livestock health and food safety.

pamphlet_excerpts: Connected Research Medicine Fields: Laboratory animal medicine and research veterinary medicine have much in common (p. 16).
Broad Scientific Skill Application: Both fields apply the skills learned in veterinary school to a number of areas of study (p. 16).
Medical Care in Research Facilities: A veterinarian working in laboratory animal medicine provides medical care for animals used in research (p. 16).
Collaborative Scientific Team Roles: The veterinarian sometimes is a member of the research team and helps design studies, interpret results, and publish articles about the research (p. 16).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Research Animal Medical Care: A veterinarian working in laboratory animal medicine provides medical care for animals used in research (p. 16).
Step 2 - Examine Study Design Collaboration: The veterinarian sometimes is a member of the research team and helps design studies, interpret results, and publish articles about the research (p. 16).
Step 3 - Review Diagnostic and Medical Innovations: Research veterinarians investigate new medicines, biotechnical and diagnostic tests, food technologies, and other new technologies (p. 16).
Step 4 - Explore Infectious Disease Surveillance: Research veterinarians might also investigate the exotic and infectious diseases that threaten public health (p. 16).
